name: Phuture
hook: Found a discontinued bass machine nobody wanted and used it completely wrong.
blurb: The Roland TB-303 was sold to guitarists as a robot bass player. It was terrible at that, so it failed and ended up cheap in secondhand shops. DJ Pierre and his friends got one without a manual, twisted the knobs while it played, and got a squelching, sliding sound nobody had heard. 'Acid Tracks' came out in 1987 and an entire genre was named after the noise. Acid house is the cleanest example on this map of a machine as the hero of the story: the sound exists because a commercial failure made the device cheap enough for people with no interest in how it was meant to be used. The Trax Records side of the story, with its famously poor pressings and disputed payments to artists, belongs to the label's own entry.
